config.title: Configuration
config.subtitle: The lists agents choose from when they file a ticket.
config.departmentsHelp: Also routes the ticket — it is assigned within the department you pick.
config.categoriesHelp: What the ticket is about. Labels only — no routing.
config.prioritiesHelp: A new priority needs its own SLA policy, or no clock will run on it.
config.channelsHelp: How the ticket arrived. Built-in ones are written by connectors and cannot be deleted.
config.customerFieldsHelp: Suggested field names for customer details. Agents can still add their own.

sla.title: SLA policies
sla.subtitle: First-response and resolution targets per priority, in hours. Leave a field blank for no target.
sla.hint: Applies to new tickets, to any ticket whose priority changes, and — when you save — to open tickets that never had a target at all. Tickets that already have deadlines keep them. The resolve clock pauses while a ticket is Pending.

storage.title: Attachment storage
storage.subtitle: Where files uploaded to tickets are kept.
storage.localHint: Files stay on the Trackly server. Simple, but they are lost if the server is replaced and they don't survive scaling to more than one instance.
storage.bucketHint: Holds attachments and logos. Must already exist, and the credential needs object read, write and delete on it.
storage.pathPrefixHint: Folder inside the bucket everything is written under, e.g. trackly. Use one if the bucket is shared with another application.
storage.cdnHint: The origin that maps onto your public bucket's root — the bucket name is not part of a CDN path.
storage.previewHeading: A logo will be served from
storage.previewNeedsBucket: Set a public bucket to see the URL.
storage.cdnScope: Trackly only ever puts workspace logos on the CDN — never a ticket attachment, because a CDN link carries no sign-in. Note that a CDN needs this bucket to be publicly readable, and attachments live in it too: Trackly never publishes their paths, but it cannot make a public bucket private. Use a separate private bucket for attachments if that matters to you.
storage.gcsKeyShape: This doesn't look like a service-account key — it needs a private_key and a client_email.
storage.storedHint: Configured. Leave blank to keep it, or paste a new one to replace it.
storage.testPassedBody: Trackly wrote a file, read it back and deleted it.
storage.switchWarning: Existing attachments stay where they are
storage.switchWarningBody: Files already uploaded remain in {{provider}} and are still served from there — but only while its credentials are kept below. Clearing them makes those attachments unreadable.

layout.title: Ticket layout
layout.subtitle: The cards in the ticket view's side panel: which are shown, and in what order.
layout.hint: Hiding a card only stops it being drawn. Nothing on the ticket changes, and switching it back on brings everything with it.

statuses.title: Statuses & workflow
statuses.subtitle: The states a ticket can be in, and which moves between them are allowed.
statuses.categoryHint: Every status sits under one of five fixed categories. The name is yours; the category is what Trackly reasons about — SLA clocks, dashboard counts and "is this ticket still open" all read the category, never the name.
statuses.empty: No statuses in this category yet.
statuses.deleteMessage: It disappears from every picker and from the workflow. Statuses that tickets are using can't be deleted — retire those instead.
statuses.recategorise: Moving a status to another category changes how Trackly treats every ticket already in it.

behaviour.open: Counts as open. SLA clocks run. A new ticket starts here.
behaviour.pending: Counts as open, but SLA clocks pause while a ticket sits here and resume with the waiting time added back on.
behaviour.active: Counts as open. SLA clocks run. Use it for work someone has actually picked up.
behaviour.resolved: Ends the ticket. Both clocks stop, a resolution note is required, and the customer gets the resolution email and the CSAT survey.
behaviour.closed: Ends the ticket. Both clocks stop and a resolution note is required, but no survey is sent.

workflow.intro: Tick a cell to allow that move. A row is where the ticket is now; a column is where it may go.
workflow.anyStatusHint: Allowed from wherever the ticket happens to be.
workflow.emptyWarning: Nothing is allowed yet, so every status change would be rejected. Trackly treats a completely empty workflow as "allow everything" instead — tick at least one cell to take control of it.
workflow.unreachable: Nothing can reach {{names}}. Agents will never be able to move a ticket into it.

catalogue.title: Registers
catalogue.subtitle: The assets, services and properties this workspace tracks on its tickets.
catalogue.noAssets: No assets yet. Add the machines, licences and equipment you support.
catalogue.noServices: No services yet. Add what your customers depend on — Payments, Email, the VPN.
catalogue.allowNew: Let agents type a new value, and remember it
catalogue.fieldsHint: Trackly's own properties — status, priority, department, category — are built in because the product reasons about them. These are yours: they are stored, shown and searched, but no rule acts on them.
catalogue.deleteFieldHint: The field and every answer to it are removed. Retiring keeps the answers and takes it off the form.

hours.title: Business hours
hours.onHint: SLA clocks only run while the desk is open. A ticket raised after hours is due from the next working morning.
hours.offHint: Clocks run round the clock. A four-hour target means four real hours, whatever the day or time.
hours.timeZoneHint: IANA name — Asia/Kolkata, Europe/London. This decides what "9am" means.
hours.invalid: Check the times on {{days}} — the closing time has to be after the opening one.
hours.existingHint: Deadlines already stamped on tickets are left alone. This changes what NEW tickets get.

scorecard.title: SLA scorecard
scorecard.empty: Nothing resolved in the last 30 days.
scorecard.hint: The last 30 days, counted from tickets each agent finished. Met / measurable — a ticket with no policy is neither met nor missed.

members.title: Members
members.subtitle: Everyone with an account here. Roles live in Trackly, never in your identity provider.
members.name: Name (optional)
members.addHint: Trackly generates a password and shows it once. Pass it on yourself — no email is sent, so this works before email is configured.
members.resetBody: A new password is generated and shown once. Their other sessions are signed out immediately.
members.deactivateBody: They are signed out everywhere and cannot sign in again until reactivated. Their tickets stay.
members.passwordIssuedBody: Give this to {{email}}. They will be asked to replace it when they first sign in.
members.passwordOnce: This is the only time it is shown. Trackly stores only a hash — if it is lost, reset it again.
members.soleAdminBody: If you lose your password and email is not working, nobody can reset it for you. Make a second person an admin.

login.title: Login methods
login.subtitle: How people sign in to this installation.
login.passwordHint: Email and password. The only method that works before email is configured.
login.passwordLocked: Cannot be turned off until another method is proven to work.
login.emailCodeHint: A magic link and a 6-digit code, sent by email.
login.emailUnproven: Not proven yet — send a test message below.
login.ssoActive: Active — someone has signed in through it.
login.ssoInactive: Not configured, or never used successfully.
login.emailProofBody: Sends a real message to your own address. Password sign-in can only be turned off once one arrives — otherwise turning it off would lock everyone out.
login.testPassedBody: Check {{email}}. If it arrived, outbound email works.
login.lockoutBody: Trackly runs on your own server — there is no support desk to call and no recovery link if the last working sign-in method is turned off. At least one proven method always stays enabled.

sso.title: Single sign-on
sso.subtitle: Let people sign in with an identity provider they already have. Roles stay in Trackly — map provider groups to roles inside each connection.
sso.emptyBody: Add one below. Everyone signs in with email and password until you do.
sso.addProviderHint: Trackly already knows each one's endpoints — you only supply the credentials from your own account.
sso.rolesBody: A provider says who someone is, never what they may do. Everyone arrives as a customer unless a group mapping says otherwise, or you change their role on the Members screen.
sso.disconnectBody: People who signed in with {{name}} will need another way in. Their tickets and accounts are kept.
sso.displayNameHint: What the sign-in button says, e.g. "Acme SSO".
sso.metadataUrlHint: Your provider publishes this. Trackly reads the signing certificate from it.
sso.metadataXmlHint: Use this when the URL is not reachable from this server.
sso.spEntityIdHint: Leave blank and Trackly generates one.
sso.spMetadataUrl: Give your provider this metadata URL
sso.tenantHint: Leave blank to admit any work account. Paste your directory ID to admit only your own organisation.
sso.tenantSlugHint: Required when several workspaces share one host. Leave blank only if this provider is reached on its own domain.
sso.baseUrlHint: Where the provider is hosted. Trackly works out the rest.
sso.secretStored: Stored — leave blank to keep it.
sso.secretOptional: Optional — leave blank for a public client using PKCE.
sso.redirectUriHint: Register this at the provider exactly as shown. A mismatch fails at the last step of a sign-in, where it is hardest to spot.
sso.acsUrlHint: Register this at the provider exactly as shown.
sso.showOnStaff: Show on the staff sign-in page
sso.showOnStaffHint: The Trackly sign-in page your team uses.
sso.showOnCustomerHint: Branded pages customers reach from your portal and submit links.
sso.allowedDomainsHint: Comma separated. Leave blank to accept any address the provider returns.
sso.openSignupBody: Anyone with an account there can sign in and will be created as a customer. Name your email domains above to narrow it.
sso.groupMappingHint: Re-evaluated on every sign-in. The highest matching role wins. Leave empty to manage roles by hand.

errors.metadata: Add the IdP metadata URL, or paste the XML.

email.title: Email
email.subtitle: How Trackly sends notifications and receives replies. Connect a provider you already use, or point it at any SMTP server. Credentials are encrypted and never shown back.
email.unprovenHeading: Nobody has proved email works yet
email.unprovenBody: Send a test message below. Until one is delivered, Trackly will not let you turn off password sign-in — an emailed code that never arrives locks everyone out permanently.
email.providersHint: Connect as many as you like. Trackly already knows each one’s servers, so you only supply the account.
email.disconnectBody: Trackly forgets {{name}}’s credentials. Anything it was sending or receiving stops until another provider takes over.
email.connectIncomplete: The provider returned an incomplete response.
email.rolesHint: Several can be connected at once; exactly one sends and at most one receives. Keeping a spare connected costs nothing.
email.sendViaHint: Notifications, sign-in codes and invitations all go this way.
email.receiveViaHint: Trackly polls this mailbox and turns messages into tickets and replies.
email.neverDelivered: No test message has been delivered yet.
email.testPassedBody: Check {{to}}. If it arrived, outbound email works.
email.fromEmailHint: Must be an address the sending provider is allowed to send as, or the message will be rejected or land in spam.
email.modeHint: Whether replying to a Trackly email does anything.

modes.oneWay: One-way — customers can reply by email
modes.twoWay: Two-way — agents and customers both reply by email

email.inboundHint: Polling reads a mailbox on a timer. A parse webhook needs an MX record pointed at your mail provider.
email.replyDomainHint: Replies come back to reply+<ticket>@ this domain.
email.webhookUrl: Point your provider’s inbound parse here
email.pollIntervalHint: Between 30 and 3600. Shorter means faster replies and more connections.
email.newTicket: Open a ticket from a cold email
email.newTicketHint: A message that matches no existing ticket starts a new one.
email.storedHint: Stored. Leave blank to keep it.
email.keepPlaceholder: Leave blank to keep the stored value
email.notificationsHint: Each one saves as you switch it.

notify.notifyCustomerOnCreate: Email the customer when their ticket is created
notify.notifyCustomerOnReply: Email the customer when an agent replies
notify.notifyCustomerOnStatus: Email the customer when the status changes
notify.notifyAgentOnAssign: Email the agent when a ticket is assigned to them
notify.notifyAgentOnReply: Email the agent when the customer replies
notify.notifyAgentOnReassign: Email the agent when a ticket is reassigned
notify.csatEnabled: Include a satisfaction survey in the resolution email

form.connectedBody: Trackly is signed in to {{account}} through {{name}}. It renews its own access; no password is stored.
form.ownAppHeading: Register Trackly in your own {{name}} account
form.ownAppBody: Trackly is self-hosted, so the app is yours, not ours. Create an OAuth client in your {{name}} console, add the redirect URI below to it, then paste the client ID and secret here.
form.redirectUriHint: Add this to your OAuth client exactly as shown. One extra character and the provider refuses the connection with an error Trackly never sees.
form.redirectUriPlatform: In Entra, add it under the Web platform — not Single-page application. A SPA redirect URI caps the refresh token at 24 hours, so inbound mail would stop every morning.
form.tenantIdHint: From your app registration's Overview page. Leave blank only if you registered it for accounts in any organisational directory — a single-tenant app is refused at the shared endpoint.
form.appPasswordBody: Prefer not to register an app? An app password from your {{name}} account works too — fill in the sending and receiving details below instead.
form.accountEmailHint: The mailbox this account owns, e.g. the address replies arrive at.
form.receivingHint: Leave blank if this provider only sends.
form.sesRegionHint: The region your SES identity is verified in, e.g. eu-west-1.
form.storedHint: Stored. Leave blank to keep it.
form.keepPlaceholder: Leave blank to keep the stored value
form.errMailbox: Fill in both the mailbox username and password, or neither.
form.errConnectOrPassword: Either connect the account, or fill in the sending details with an app password.

templates.title: Email templates
templates.subtitle: The subject and body of every message Trackly sends. Edit one of them, or edit the shared layout to restyle all of them at once.
templates.emptyBody: The server returned an empty catalogue, which should not happen. Try again — if it persists, the API is on a different version from this page.
templates.layoutHint: The frame every email is rendered into — logo, colours and footer. Editing it changes all of them at once.
templates.messagesHint: Each one is the content of an email. Unless it skips the layout, it is rendered into the frame above.
templates.testHint: Each Test button sends that one template with sample data. It is not the delivery proof Trackly asks for before password sign-in can be turned off — that stays on the test on the Email page.
templates.testToHint: Leave blank to send it to your own address.
templates.testDraftHint: Sends what is on screen, saved or not.
templates.testPassedBody: Sent to {{to}}. Delivery can take a minute.
templates.resetBody: Your version is deleted and Trackly goes back to the one it ships with. This cannot be undone.
templates.resetDone: {{name}} is back to the built-in version
templates.subject: Subject
templates.bodyHint: HTML exactly as it will be sent. Click a variable on the right to insert it at the cursor.
templates.standaloneHint: Skip the shared layout and send this body as the whole email. For a finished HTML email from a designer.
templates.useCustomHint: Off keeps your draft but sends the built-in instead. It never stops the email going out.
templates.previewHint: Rendered by the server with sample data, through the same code that sends real mail.
templates.variablesHint: Click one to insert it at the cursor.
templates.requiredHint: Required — this template cannot be saved without it
templates.requiredNote: Required: {{names}}. A save that drops one is refused: on a self-hosted install an email that cannot do its job is a permanent lockout.
templates.escapingNote: Double braces escape the value; triple braces insert it as HTML. Scripts, iframes and event handlers are removed when you save.

rewards.title: Rewards
rewards.subtitle: Targets your workspace counts as good work. Every one is measured from data Trackly already records — nothing extra for agents to log.
rewards.empty: No goals yet. Add one below and agents start earning it from their next resolved ticket.
rewards.name: Name
rewards.minimumSampleHint: A rate needs a floor: one ticket answered inside SLA is 100%, and without a minimum it would out-rank 96% across two hundred.
rewards.sweepHint: Goals are checked every 15 minutes. A badge is given the moment its target is reached, not when the period ends.

confirmDelete.heading: Delete this goal?
confirmDelete.message: Nobody has earned "{{name}}", so nothing is lost. Retire it instead if you may want it back.

widget.title: Widget
widget.subtitle: The chat widget your customers see on your own site.
widget.emptyBody: Create one to get a snippet you can paste into your site.
widget.name: Name
widget.taglineHint: Shown under the greeting on the home view.
widget.greetingHint: Followed by the visitor's first name when Trackly knows it.
widget.teamHint: Conversations from this widget are routed to this team.
widget.themeHint: Overrides the workspace colour for this widget only. Clear to inherit.
widget.launchHint: Defaults. A host page can override any of these per page.
widget.activeHint: An inactive widget stops loading everywhere it is embedded.
widget.hideLauncherHint: The site opens the panel from its own button instead.
widget.launchWidget: Open the panel on first load
widget.showFormHint: Skipped when the host page already identifies them.
widget.identityHint: The widget token is public. A signed token is what proves a visitor is who the page says they are.
widget.identityEnable: Require a signed token for identity
widget.secretHint: Sign a JWT with this on your server. Regenerating stops every page using the old key immediately.
widget.regenerateBody: Every page signing tokens with the current key stops verifying at once. There is no overlap window.
widget.secretOnceBody: This is the only time it is shown. If you lose it, regenerate.
widget.verifyJwtHint: Paste a token your server signed and Trackly will say whether it would accept it.
widget.requireEmailHint: Visitors confirm an emailed code before they can start a conversation.
widget.domainsHint: One origin per line. Only these sites can load this widget.
widget.domainsEmpty: Leave empty to allow any site.
widget.deleteBody: Every page embedding “{{name}}” stops working. Conversations it raised stay in the queue.
widget.brandingScopeHeading: These apply everywhere, not just to this widget
widget.brandingScopeBody: Your logo, footer and workspace colour are worn by the sign-in page, the portal, the knowledge base and the header of every email Trackly sends. Widget theme, on the Configuration tab, overrides the colour for this widget alone.
widget.logoHint: PNG, SVG, JPEG or WebP, up to 1 MB.
widget.defaultColourHint: Used by every surface that has no colour of its own.
widget.footerTextHint: Shown at the bottom of customer-facing pages.
widget.hidePoweredByHint: Removes it from the widget, the portal and the knowledge base.
widget.snippetHint: Paste this just before the closing body tag.
widget.mobileBody: Native apps can open the panel URL in a web view. A proper SDK is not built.
widget.variables: What a host page can send
widget.variablesHint: All optional. Set them in the config object beside the snippet.
widget.varUniqueId: Your own id for this person. Must match the signed token when identity verification is on.
widget.varContact: Name, email and phone. Pre-fills the details form.
widget.varToken: A JWT signed with the secret key above. The only thing that proves an identity.
widget.varBag: Free-form key/value pairs stored against the contact.

customers.name: Name
customers.emailLocked: The email identifies this customer and cannot be changed here.
customers.customFieldsHelp: Anything your business tracks about this customer.
customers.noTickets: No tickets from this customer yet.
customers.fieldsHelp: Suggested field names for customer details. Agents can still add their own.
customers.title: Customers
customers.subtitle: Everyone who raises tickets — and who has found the portal.
customers.alreadyExists: Already on the list — {{name}} was there, so nothing was added.
customers.searchPlaceholder: Search by name, email, phone or company…

empty.body: They are created the first time somebody emails the desk or submits the form — or add one here.
empty.filteredBody: Try a different search, or clear the sign-in filter.

types.sla_warning: An SLA is about to run out
types.unblocked: unblocked a ticket you are on

setup.title: Set up Trackly
setup.subtitle: This installation is new. Create your workspace and you'll be signed in as its administrator.
setup.organisationHint: Shown to your customers on the support portal, forms and emails.
setup.emailHint: You'll be the first administrator. Sign in later with a link sent to this address.
setup.name: Your name (optional)
setup.footnote: You're signed in straight away — email isn't configured yet, so there's no link to send.

panel.title: One workspace. Yours.
panel.body: Trackly runs on your own infrastructure. No tenant to pick, no domain to verify — set a name and start taking tickets.

setup.passwordHint: At least {{min}} characters. This is how you sign in from now on.

password.title: Change your password
password.subtitle: Choose something only you know.
password.forcedSubtitle: You signed in with a temporary password someone else issued. Replace it before you continue.

panel.title: Your account, your key.
panel.body: Trackly stores only a hash — nobody, including an administrator, can read your password back.

tasks.title: My tasks
tasks.subtitleMine: Every open step assigned to {{name}}, across all tickets.
tasks.subtitleAll: Every open step on the team, across all tickets.

filters.hint: Tasks on resolved tickets are hidden.

empty.heading: Nothing on your list
empty.body: Tasks you add to a ticket, or that a colleague assigns you, show up here.
empty.filteredBody: Try a different owner, or include finished tasks.

assets.title: Assets
assets.subtitle: What the workspace owns, who has it, and what it has cost in tickets.
assets.searchPlaceholder: Search by name or asset tag…
assets.noHistory: No ticket has ever been raised about this asset.

empty.heading: No assets yet

empty.filteredBody: Try a different name or asset tag.

services.title: Services
services.subtitle: What customers depend on, and what is broken right now.
services.noReports: No open ticket says this service is affected.

empty.heading: No services yet

home.emptyBody: Start one and we will reply here.

details.heading: Tell us who you are
details.body: So we can reply and keep your conversations together.
details.name: Name

thread.newBody: Type below and we will pick it up.
